arxiv-1809-00275.title: Dagger linear logic for categorical quantum mechanics Thanks: Partially supported by NSERC, Canada
arxiv-1809-00275.creator: Robin Cockett \rsuper a, Cole Comfort \rsuper b, Priyaa V. Srinivasan \rsuper a
arxiv-1809-00275.description: Abstract . Categorical quantum mechanics exploits the dagger compact closed structure of finite dimensional Hilbert spaces, and uses the graphical calculus of string diagrams to facilitate reasoning about finite dimensional processes. A significant portion of quantum physics, however, involves reasoning about infinite dimensional processes, and it is well-known that the category of all Hilbert spaces is not compact closed.

arxiv-2307-00842.title: VINECS: Video-based Neural Character Skinning
arxiv-2307-00842.creator: Zhouyingcheng Liao, Vladislav Golyanik, Marc Habermann, Christian Theobalt
arxiv-2307-00842.description: Abstract Rigging and skinning clothed human avatars is a challenging task and traditionally requires a lot of manual work and expertise. Recent methods addressing it either generalize across different characters or focus on capturing the dynamics of a single character observed under different pose configurations.

arxiv-2401-03932.title: Using reinforcement learning to improve drone-based inference of greenhouse gas fluxes
arxiv-2401-03932.creator: Alouette van Hove, Kristoffer Aalstad 1 and Norbert Pirk 1
arxiv-2401-03932.description: Abstract Accurate mapping of greenhouse gas fluxes at the Earth’s surface is essential for the validation and calibration of climate models. In this study, we present a framework for surface flux estimation with drones. Our approach uses data assimilation (DA) to infer fluxes from drone-based observations, and reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the drone’s sampling strategy.

arxiv-2403-16712.title: Chase Termination Beyond Polynomial Time Thanks: This paper is the technical report for the paper with the same title appearing in the Proceedings of the 43rd Symposium on Principles of Database Systems (PODS’24) ( Hanisch and Krötzsch 2024 ) . CCS: Theory of computation Constraint and logic program
arxiv-2403-16712.creator: Philipp Hanisch, Markus Krötzsch
arxiv-2403-16712.description: Abstract . The chase is a widely implemented approach to reason with tuple-generating dependencies (tgds), used in data exchange, data integration, and ontology-based query answering. However, it is merely a semi-decision procedure, which may fail to terminate. Many decidable conditions have been proposed for tgds to ensure chase termination, typically by forbidding some kind of “cycle” in the chase process.

arxiv-2508-21060.title: Multi-View 3D Point Tracking
arxiv-2508-21060.creator: Frano Rajič, Haofei Xu, Marko Mihajlovic, Siyuan Li, Irem Demir, Emircan Gündoğdu Lei Ke Sergey Prokudin Marc Pollefeys Siyu Tang, [0.75ex] ETH Zürich Carnegie Mellon University Balgrist University Hospital Microsoft
arxiv-2508-21060.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Frano Rajič, Haofei Xu, Marko Mihajlovic, Siyuan Li, Irem Demir, Emircan Gündoğdu Lei Ke Sergey Prokudin Marc Pollefeys Siyu Tang, [0.75ex] ETH Zürich Carnegie Mellon University Balgrist University Hospital Microsoft. arxiv-2602-16603.title: FlowPrefill: Decoupling Preemption from Prefill Scheduling Granularity to Mitigate Head-of-Line Blocking in LLM Serving DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/0
arxiv-2602-16603.creator: Chia-chi Hsieh, Zan Zong, Xinyang Chen, Jianjiang Li, Jidong Zhai, Lijie Wen
arxiv-2602-16603.description: Abstract . The growing demand for large language models (LLMs) requires serving systems to handle many concurrent requests with diverse service level objectives (SLOs). This exacerbates head-of-line (HoL) blocking during the compute-intensive prefill phase, where long-running requests monopolize resources and delay higher-priority ones, leading to widespread time-to-first-token (TTFT) SLO violations.

pmc-10536022.title: Simple Coumarin-Based Fluorescent Probe for Recognition of Pd(II) and Its Live Cell Imaging
pmc-10536022.creator: Xiangyang Zhang, Yaodan Xu, Youming Shen, Feifei Wang
pmc-10536022.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A simple coumarin hydrazine Schiff base bearing a thioether recognition fragment (compound CBBS) has been rationally designed and easily prepared. CBBS exhibited an excellent selectivity for Pd(II) and a low detection limit of 65 nM (S/N = 3). The fluorescence emission intensities of CBBS at 495 nm were linear to Pd(II) concentrations in a wide range from 0 to 80 μM. Moreover, CBBS has been well used in fluorescence imaging of Pd(II) in living A549 cells.

pmc-11665912.title: Dark continuous noise from visual pigment as a major mechanism underlying rod–cone difference in light sensitivity
pmc-11665912.creator: Zuying Chai, Daniel Silverman, Sihan Li, Parinaz Bina, King-Wai Yau
pmc-11665912.description: SignificanceRetinal rods exhibit two kinds of dark spontaneous phototransduction activity. One is quantal noise originating from thermal isomerization of rhodopsin. The other is continuous noise believed for almost three decades to come from intrinsic activity of the phosphodiesterase enzyme mediating phototransduction. The rod quantal noise dictates the scotopic light threshold, but what limits the photopic light threshold remains unclear.

pmc-13236819.title: Butterfly gliomas: to biopsy or to ablate – a longitudinal cohort study
pmc-13236819.creator: Vratko Himic, Morgan Leigh Johnson, Anshul Ratnaparkhi, Roxanne C Mayrand, Jay Chandar, Vaidya Govindarajan, Daniel C Kreatsoulas, Arman Jahangiri, Zachary C Gersey, Daniel M Aaronson, Ricardo J Komotar, Micheal E Ivan, Ashish H Shah
pmc-13236819.description: PurposeButterfly gliomas are an aggressive subset of high-grade glioma characterized by bilateral hemispheric involvement. These patients often only receive biopsy followed by chemoradiation rather than surgical resection. Laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) provides a minimally invasive alternative that can improve survival.MethodsWe retrospectively compare outcomes in biopsy alone versus LITT cohorts. Demographic characteristics, perioperative outcomes, and survival metrics were analyzed.
